title: Parastichy counts on fir-cones are nearly constant within a species

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Parastichy counts on fir-cones are nearly constant within a species

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The numbers of conspicuous parastichies on fir-cones are on the whole very constant within a species, e.g. 5 and 3 in the Norway spruce and 8 and 5 in the common larch.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIV: On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: and among fir-cones, we can easily count these, and we find them to be on the whole very constant in number, according to the species.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XIV, “On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis”; topic “Numbers of parastichies”. Scope: cones of conifers

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch14-04: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.84

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Counts and species identity are direct variables, and public specimen imagery can yield large samples. The named examples and constancy criterion provide clear confirming and refuting outcomes.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Count opposing parastichy families in many georeferenced cones per conifer species and estimate within-species frequency distributions, explicitly checking the stated 5/3 spruce and 8/5 larch modes. Tight species-specific modes support the claim; broad variation or different dominant counts refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Images must show the cone at sufficient resolution and orientation.

Cultivar, age and cone position may contribute within-species variation.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.75
operationalizability: 0.97
analysis feasibility: 0.88
data adequacy: 0.68
discriminating power: 0.94

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Within-species constancy of parastichy number is a straightforward count, and the examples are specific enough to check. The large samples that exist were published as summaries rather than deposited as specimen-level data, and open cone imaging covers too few species to replace them. A team could re-count a modest image sample, but the full species-level claim still depends on compiling scattered studies.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Count the conspicuous parastichy pairs on many cones per species, including Norway spruce and larch, and partition the variance within and among species. Constancy is supported if one pair dominates each species, such as 5 and 3 in spruce and 8 and 5 in larch; frequent within-species switching among distant pairs would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cone size varies within species, which Thompson elsewhere expects to change the visible pair.

Large published cone counts (pines, larches, spruces) are summarized in papers and are not one open raw file.
